Space Exploration: From Sputnik to Mars & Beyond

Tracing evolution from Cold War competition to commercial collaboration

October 28, 2026

HISTORICAL CONTEXT

The Dawn of the Space Age: Sputnik and Explorer 1

  • The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 on October 4, 1957, triggering global geopolitical anxiety.
  • The United States responded with Explorer 1 launch on January 31, 1958 to restore technological prestige.
  • Explorer 1 operated for 105 days, transmitting critical cosmic radiation data from orbit.
  • Mission directly led to discovery of Van Allen radiation belts, redefining near-Earth space science.

GOVERNANCE

Legacy Space vs. New Space Governance Models

Dimension Legacy Space (1957–2000s) New Space (2010s–Present)
Funding Model State-dominated budgets driven by geopolitical competition Public-private partnerships aligning goals with private expertise
Innovation Cycle Slower development timelines due to bureaucratic oversight Rapid innovation cycles driven by commercial entities
Cost Structure High costs associated with expendable launch hardware Significant cost reduction through reusable technology
Regulatory Focus Primary focus on national security and prestige Evolving frameworks addressing environmental pollution and monopolization

The Next Decade: 2025–2035

From temporary visits to permanent infrastructure: establishing the lunar gateway and preparing for the Martian surface.

LUNAR RETURN

Artemis Program: Returning to the Moon

  • Artemis II successfully launched April 2026 marking first crewed Orion flight
  • NASA accelerated plans October 2026 targeting lunar surface return by 2028
  • Program focuses on sustainability rather than just flag-planting footprint activities
  • In-situ resource utilization will extract water ice for fuel and life support
Lunar Gateway will serve as staging point for deeper solar system exploration

MISSION ARCHITECTURE

Challenges of Crewed Mars Missions

1

Transit Hazards

Months-long travel demands advanced radiation shielding for crew safety.

2

Life Support

Closed-loop ecological systems must sustain crew without any resupply.

3

Mars Landing

Supersonic retro-propulsion techniques are required for heavy payload delivery.

4

Political Will

Bureaucratic pressures historically limit the long-term planning required.

EMERGING POWER

Korea's Emerging Space Capabilities

Nuri Rocket (KSLV-II)

  • Achieved independent launch capability through successful domestic development
  • Established South Korea as a sovereign space-faring nation

Danuri Lunar Orbiter

  • Surveys lunar resources including water ice and helium-3
  • Maps topography to select future landing sites for partners

Summary & Future Outlook

  • • Space exploration evolved from bipolar geopolitical race to commercial endeavor
  • • Reusable rockets drastically lowered launch costs enabling sustainable models
  • • Next decade focuses on lunar sustainability via Artemis and Mars prep
  • • Emerging nations like South Korea contribute to lunar science and capabilities
  • • New legal and ethical frameworks required to manage commercial activities
